reason: I’ll start making paper for the gallery; soaking plant fiber in water seems like a useful first step.
expectation: I expect wet fiber or pulp that can be made into paper.

alternatives.reason: Glass and stone might start the mosaic, but I chose to work on paper first.

effect: The plant fiber and water made paper pulp, so I can continue toward paper.
reason: Combining pulp with cloth looks like the next step in making paper.
expectation: I expect a sheet of paper, perhaps formed or dried using the cloth.

effect: The pulp and cloth made paper, completing that part of the gallery preparation.
reason: Dye and a bowl may prepare paint for the paper.
expectation: I expect a bowl of paint or another coloring material.

alternatives.reason: Glass and stone may prepare pieces for the mosaic, but I want to continue toward a painting.

effect: The dye and bowl made paint, which can now be used with the paper.
reason: Paint and paper should make a picture for the gallery.
expectation: I expect a painting or painted paper.

effect: The paint and paper made a picture, ready for the gallery.
reason: Stone and brick seem useful for building a gallery to display the picture.
expectation: I expect a building or structure for the gallery.

alternatives.reason: Glass and stone might prepare pieces for the mosaic, but I want to build the gallery first.

effect: Stone and brick made an arch, suggesting a structural step toward the gallery.
reaction: The arch was more specific than I expected.
reason: Adding planks to the arch may complete a gallery structure for the picture.
expectation: I expect a building or display structure, though it may need another step.

alternatives.reason: Glass and stone may start the mosaic, but I want to finish the gallery first.

effect: The arch and planks made an arcade, which can now hold the picture.
reaction: The arcade is a plausible gallery structure.
reason: Adding the picture to the arcade should complete the gallery.
expectation: I expect a gallery displaying the picture.

effect: The picture completed the gallery, leaving the mosaic goal.
reaction: The gallery came together as expected.
reason: Glass and stone may produce pieces for the mosaic.
expectation: I expect small glass pieces or another material for assembling the mosaic.

alternatives.reason: Glass and planks might also lead toward the mosaic, but stone seems more useful for breaking glass into pieces.

effect: Glass and stone made mosaic pieces, which can now be set into clay.
reaction: Breaking the glass into pieces matched my expectation.
reason: Clay looks like a backing for the mosaic pieces and should advance the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect a mosaic made by setting the pieces into clay.

effect: The mosaic pieces set into clay completed the remaining goal and the chapter.
reaction: The finished mosaic matched my expectation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the arcade and adding the picture was the most worthwhile sequence: the separate paper, paint and construction steps came together as a gallery.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making paint and then applying it to paper was predictable and held little surprise.

surprise.text: Stone and brick produced an arch, a more specific structural component than I expected.

arbitrary.text: Combining an arch with planks to make an arcade felt somewhat unclear; the result did not explain how the planks formed it.

continue.text: I would probably stop here. The gallery and mosaic came together coherently, but the offered combinations made the decisions fairly predictable.
